We hear it all the time... "I can't lose weight, I have a medical condishun".

Here's the thing- all my life, I have agreed with it, but not how they use it. I'm not saying that I gain weight for no reason, because that is physically impossible. I've always been the light eater. I never get hungry, but I drink water constantly. I mentioned it to my doctor and he gave the answer I was expecting... "It's got to be your math. Track your food, don't lie about it, and we will see". So, I tracked my food. I scanned everything I ate, I added in every last little morsel that crossed my lips.

I eat between 600 and 900 calories a day. I don't get hungry, I don't deny myself healthy food (or the occasional junk meal). To me, my eating is totally normal. I also jog (trying to work up to running) and work out, and play with my 7 year old (child and dog).

I really want to get my metabolism tested, but right now it just isn't happening. Maybe this summer. I just wondered what y'all thought.
Honest opinions and/or hard data... those with thyroid issues, does it impact your metabolism?

What most people refer to in this context is Hypothyroidism. It is a malfunction of your hormonal system that can indeed lead to weight gain. Emphasis on can.

Like every chronic or permanent condition, it requires discipline to live with. It makes it easier for people to accumulate weight and harder for them to lose it. But it is still no excuse. You can be lean with an impaired thyroid.

On an unrelated note: Metabolism tested? What exactly do you mean by that? I would appreciate any and all information.

You are not. You just have good habits. I have to work with people suffering from some sort of metabolic disease and there are all kinds of cases. We had a dude with hyperthyroidism who was morbidly obese.
